title: Count Cells in Overlapping Horizontal and Vertical Substrings
summary: Given an m x n matrix grid and a string pattern, count the number of cells that are part of at least one matching horizontal and one matching vertical substring of the pattern.
statement: Given an m x n matrix grid and a string pattern, count the number of cells that are part of at least one matching horizontal and one matching vertical substring of the pattern. A horizontal substring reads left to right, wrapping to the next row if necessary, and a vertical substring reads top to bottom, wrapping to the next column if necessary.
constraints: grid has at most 100,000 cells and pattern length is at most the cell count.
Horizontal reading is row-major and vertical reading is column-major; neither order wraps after its final cell.
Count cells covered by at least one pattern match in both reading orders.
hints: The wrapping rules are simply substring matches in row-major and column-major flattened strings.
Use KMP to find every match, difference arrays to mark full matched ranges, then map each cell between the two flattenings.
Build coverage booleans for both flattened strings and count row-major cells whose corresponding column-major position is also covered.
KMP finds all overlapping matches, range differences mark their union, and the index mapping identifies the same physical cell.
editorial: KMP finds all overlapping matches, range differences mark their union, and the index mapping identifies the same physical cell.

tests.explanation: The single row-major and column-major matches overlap at exactly one cell.
All matches together cover four cells in both reading directions.
